question: Do provided ERP features improve held-person next-round choice prediction beyond the specified history for frozen matched procedures?
descriptive_estimand: Equal-person mean of history log loss minus all-ERP log loss on the same 816 queries; seven people, each weighted 1/7.

matched_history_ERP_control.proof: H includes episode and round; admitted participant:episode:round is unique, so exact within-person full-H strata are singletons.

future_null_design_unselected.all_ERP_beyond_H: Seven-dimensional ERP vector jointly conditional on H.
future_null_design_unselected.offer_beyond_prestimulus: Four offer terms jointly conditional on H and the three fixed baselines.
requires: Justified conditional joint distribution and sequential dependence model.
Training-only estimation and separately selected fitting/refitting policy.
Validity and model-misspecification sensitivity; no arbitrary bins or assumed exchangeability.

sensitivity: Seven leave-one-person-out descriptive means only; no refit, confidence interval, subset choice, or new assignment. Primary retains all seven.
upstream_admission_required: Exact preparation and split/source identity admission.
Independently fixed full target-free schedule, not candidate-selected support.
Canonical support checked before view masking.
Same training-only modeling and tuning policy across views.
All 21 protocols, predictions and custody admitted before protected scoring.
Original score report retained; scalar receipt fields are not provenance proof.
scientific_limits: Exposed development people, not an unexposed confirmation cohort.
Next-round prediction extends the published same-row choice endpoint.
Offline positional ERP linkage does not establish independent epoch identity or online availability.
Predictive procedure comparison, not causal effect or intrinsic neural information.
No conditional-independence test, scientific success threshold, confidence interval or p-value.

public_distribution.implementation: Independently authored Python standard-library pure adapter and invented engineering tests.
